newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Aeroflot hopes to resume Moscow-Riga route.
newsitem.headline: Aeroflot hopes to resume Moscow-Riga route.

text.p: Russia's Aeroflot International Airlines hopes to resume regular flights between Moscow and the Latvian capital Riga after a scheduling row stopped them, a senior company official said on Wednesday.

Gennady Danilychev, director of Aeroflot's Commonwealth of Independent States and Baltics department, said the company had ceased flights to Riga on October 31 after Latvian aviation authorities failed to confirm Aeroflot's winter schedule.
"We have not given up on restoring service to this route," he said, adding that talks between Russia's Federal Aviation Service (FAS) and the Latvian Transport Ministry were in progress.
FAS officials were not immediately available for comment.
Aeroflot had planned to fly the route thrice weekly on Tupolev-134 jets from November. It serviced the route four times a week before the row.
Russia's private Transaero and Latvia's private RiAir fly between Moscow and Riga and have a code-sharing agreement.
